ranked.headline: Computational correction of batch effects and missing values in single-cell omics data
ranked.summary: Several frameworks posted in May 2026 unify batch correction, imputation, and integration assessment for single-cell and bulk omics data.

ranked.headline: Pangenome graphs and long-read assemblies resolve hidden human structural variation
ranked.summary: Graph-based NUMT detection reports 2.52-fold better sensitivity, and HPRC long-read assemblies now enable allele-level catalogs of LINE-1 and SVs.

ranked.headline: Learned models link histology, spatial transcriptomics, and perturbation responses
ranked.summary: Spatial and single-cell transcriptomics are increasingly modeled with histology, perturbation, and graph-based learning frameworks.

ranked.headline: Pulldown probes and assembly artifacts challenge how RNA measurements are interpreted
ranked.summary: A meta-analysis attributes lncRNA-chromatin binding to DNA off-targeting while long-read tools refine transcript assembly and multiplexed nanopore sequencing…

ranked.headline: Read-based workflows and benchmarks for microbial and strain-level pathogen detection
ranked.summary: Short- and long-read benchmarks now test strain profiling and full-length amplicon classification across mock and natural communities.

ranked.headline: Dynamical models and flow matching infer biological dynamics from sparse, static data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints combine optimal transport, flow matching and ODE models to infer dynamics from static or sparse biological data.

ranked.headline: Open-source tools automate omics analysis from imaging, proteomics, and sequence data
ranked.summary: Turnkey, interface-accessible pipelines now package established omics tools for reproducible analysis across several modalities.

ranked.headline: Automated software for parametrizing and building biomolecular structure models
ranked.summary: Recent papers and a preprint package force field parametrization, DNA and peptide model building, and simulation input generation into software tools.

ranked.headline: Deep models condition on cell state and perturbation biology beyond molecular structure
ranked.summary: Recent preprints attribute drug-blind prediction plateaus to metric artifacts and push biological state into model architectures and training objectives.

ranked.headline: Population priors and structured models for clinical prediction from limited data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published COPD study pair explicit priors, covariates, or pretraining with clinical and omics models for limited-data prediction.

ranked.headline: Learned models and simulators advance variant interpretation and genomic analysis
ranked.summary: Foundation models and ML classifiers are now being packaged as applied tools for clinical variant triage, tumor profiling and CRISPR screen design.

ranked.headline: Pretrained embeddings drive prediction of microbial genomic and protein properties
ranked.summary: Genome language models are now benchmarked explicitly, and protein-trained representations are being transferred to nucleotide and effector-prediction tasks.

ranked.headline: Sparse autoencoders steer pretrained protein and genomic language model representations
ranked.summary: Pretrained protein and genomic language models are being interpreted, steered, and extended for variant, PTM, and interaction prediction.

ranked.headline: AI-linked spatial omics maps kidney glycans and diabetic heart lipid dysregulation
ranked.summary: Spatially anchored AI and multi-omics readouts are moving tissue-scale molecular profiling toward defined disease-relevant units.

ranked.headline: Genome-scale models predict microbial cross-feeding, growth laws, and product yield
ranked.summary: Constraint-based and dynamic models now extend from microbial communities to cross-species growth laws and engineered production strains.

ranked.headline: Pretrained biological representations reused for protein, DNA and ligand prediction
ranked.summary: Multimodal and structure-aware pretraining now extends sequence foundation models to affinity, variant interpretation and function prediction.

ranked.headline: Open-source computational tools expand screening, refinement, and free-energy workflows
ranked.summary: Blinded benchmarking and new open-source releases now test screening and free-energy methods against explicit accuracy and leakage constraints.

ranked.headline: Sequencing tools are benchmarked on simulated and real reads across difficult loci
Biomolecular network structure inferred from heterogeneous, high-dimensional measurements
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs heterogeneity-aware DAG learning with multi-tissue eQTL-based causal inference to map disease genes and network structure.

ranked.headline: Recovering cell-state dynamics and regulatory kinetics from single-cell snapshots
ranked.summary: Cross-sectional single-cell and spatial data lack time resolution, so new methods infer transitions and regulatory dynamics from snapshots.

ranked.headline: Pangenome graphs and network alignment reveal method-dependent genomic conclusions
ranked.summary: Inference choices in pangenome and network analysis are now tested for their effects on GWAS loci, gene family evolution, and regulatory module detection.

ranked.headline: First-passage timing separable from steady-state output in stochastic regulatory models
ranked.summary: Recent work treats first-passage timing and steady-state output as separable in stochastic regulatory models, including phage lysis decisions.

ranked.headline: Learned models prioritise sequences for experimental testing in molecular recognition
ranked.summary: Computational models now select or generate sequences for wet-lab characterisation across antibody, aptamer, and protein specificity problems.

ranked.headline: Quantitative TF-DNA affinity models and motif comparison beyond PWM representations
ranked.summary: High-throughput Kd measurements and deep learning are moving TF binding models beyond pairwise-additive motif representations.

ranked.headline: Contiguous reference genomes for a lizard, a cleptoparasitic bee and an invasive plant
ranked.summary: Endangered and invasive taxa now have high-contiguity assemblies, enabling comparative analyses of gene family dynamics and synteny.

ranked.headline: Structure-aware models sharpen causal variant and centromere inference from genomic data
ranked.summary: Explicit structural priors in transformer and graph models now improve centromere mapping and GWAS fine-mapping from weak evidence.

ranked.headline: Automated conformational ensembles benchmarked against free energy, NMR, and docking data
ranked.summary: Current work pairs conformational sampling with quantitative validation against experimental or quantum references across drug and macrocycle targets.

ranked.headline: Bayesian models infer transmission networks from genetic and epidemiological data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications explicitly couple within-host, genetic and population-level data within transmission and epidemic inference.

ranked.headline: Interpretable fMRI models test selectivity and shared geometry of human visual cortex
ranked.summary: Recent preprints move encoding-model evaluation beyond predictive accuracy toward internal mechanisms, recovery structure, and cross-subject geometry.

ranked.headline: Calibrated and privacy-aware prediction models for sparse biomedical data
ranked.summary: Clinical and pharmacological datasets are sparse, fragmented, or privacy-restricted, motivating calibrated and robust modeling approaches.

ranked.headline: Bayesian models link within-host kinetics and latent infection risk to transmission
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published study apply Bayesian latent-state models to link within-host measurements with infection and transmission dynamics.

ranked.headline: Explicit gene and spatial scaffolds in generative models of noisy single-cell data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications add explicit gene-level or spatial structure to diffusion, graph, and autoencoder models of single-cell and spatial data.

ranked.headline: Geometric partitions and topological summaries guide inference in biological models
ranked.summary: Geometric and topological treatments of model parameter and state spaces are now applied to agent-based, ODE, and ecological network models.

ranked.headline: Deep learning on sequencing reads detects non-canonical DNA bases and methylation states
ranked.summary: Read-level models now infer DNA lesions, non-canonical bases, and methylation directly from nanopore and cell-free DNA data.

ranked.headline: Single-cell profiles map age-linked T-cell shifts, LINE-1 senescence and demyelination
ranked.summary: Paired and atlas-scale single-cell data now resolve age-linked immune and glial states at isoform, locus and regulatory resolution.

ranked.headline: Transformer and flow models advance de novo peptide sequencing from MS/MS spectra
ranked.summary: Recent models add zero-shot open PTM discovery and non-autoregressive decoding to spectrum-based peptide sequencing, alongside learned retention-time…

ranked.headline: Plasticity and heterogeneity shape adaptive therapy and viral coevolution dynamics
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a publication model how plasticity and heterogeneity govern relapse, aging, and viral coevolution.

ranked.headline: Spiking neuron models now encode timing, fit conductances, and classify spike trains
ranked.summary: Data-driven fitting of spiking and conductance-based neuron models is being linked to sequence timing, LFP rhythms, and spike-train classification.

ranked.headline: Molecular dynamics resolves active-state and free-energy landscapes across three systems
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a 2026 study use MD to test whether predicted models and docked complexes sample the conformational states their structures imply.

ranked.headline: Site-level roll-up and cleavable cross-linkers sharpen structural proteomics readouts
ranked.summary: Recent benchmarks and MS-cleavable cross-linkers address site-level accuracy in bottom-up structural proteomics readouts.
